postings.title: Accounting Analyst
postings.text:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Join us to solve real world problems while shaping the future of global trade.

The Opportunity:

Flexport has an immediate opening for an Accounting Analyst to join our Finance team. Finance plays a central role in our success by creating transparency of the company's performance, financials, risks, and internal controls, and building the people, process, and product needed for the future of Flexport. We are seeking a highly motivated Accounting Analyst with a mission to recommend and drive new initiatives and support our fast-growing organization. As an Accounting Analyst, you will have the opportunity to build personalized relationships with key stakeholders across multiple functional departments within our dynamic finance organization. Your innovative ideas and results-oriented approach will be essential to our continued success, and you will play a critical role in driving improvement and innovation as we grow.

You will

• Record and maintain journal entries (“JEs”) to ensure accuracy in the general ledger

• Collaborate with Operations and AP teams to ensure data accuracy and monthly accruals

• Key contributor in the monthly close processes for accounting team by preparing journal entries and reconciliations

• Update and maintain the company's accounting Standard Operating Procedures (“SOPs”) for assigned areas, ensuring compliance with evolving business processes and accounting standards

• Assist with prepaid schedules, and maintain assigned balance sheet accounts accuracy

• Assist with lease schedules and support JE generations

• Assist with Treasury team on payments initiations and processing

• Support variance analysis and provide commentary on P&L movements

• Help identify process improvements that streamline month-end closing and reporting processes, maximizing efficiency and accuracy, and support automation initiatives

You should have

• Strong business level English

• Bachelor's Degree or above in Accounting, Finance, or a related field

• 2+ years of working experience in public accounting (preferably Big 4) and/or in an accounting function with strong understanding of accounting

• High attention to detail and problem-solving ability with a keen focus on continuous improvement

• Prioritization skills and the ability to execute on deliverables in a fast-paced and results-oriented environment

• A willingness to embrace and drive changes

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

• Strong Excel skills

What You'll Do

Collections & Account Management

postings.text:
About Flexport:

Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

The Opportunity

We’re looking for an Accounts Receivable Collections Analyst to manage a portfolio of customer accounts and help collect payments on time. You’ll investigate overdue balances, resolve payment issues, and build relationships with customers’ Accounts Payable teams.

This role calls for persistence, careful analysis, and good judgment in sensitive conversations. You’ll work with teams across Flexport and use AI and automation to improve daily collections work. The role reports to the Head of North American Collections.

You Will

• Manage collections for assigned accounts through email and phone outreach. Prioritize overdue balances and follow through on commitments to help meet cash collection and days sales outstanding (DSO) targets.

• Review account aging and collection activity daily. Keep records of customer conversations, payment promises, disputes, and next steps accurate and up to date.

• Build relationships with customers’ Accounts Payable teams and act as their point of contact for collections and payment questions.

• Coordinate incoming requests and handle initial escalations. Resolve issues promptly and bring in the right team when a problem needs further review.

• Investigate complex account balances and recommend next steps based on the facts, customer history, and payment risk.

• Research invoice and payment discrepancies, reconcile account information, and work with the appropriate teams to resolve customers’ AR/AP questions.

• Work with Credit to arrange and monitor approved payment schedules for overdue accounts.

• Lead biweekly reviews with business leaders on open receivables, collection risks, and the actions needed to resolve them.

• Work with Credit, Account Management, Sales, Disputes, and Legal to resolve issues that delay payment while maintaining professional customer relationships.

• Use approved AI tools to summarize account histories, analyze aging data, and draft follow-ups. Verify amounts and claims before acting, protect customer information, and work with the AR manager to test and document process improvements.

• Support Finance and Accounting with month-end close activities, accurate account records, and other projects as needed.

Success in Your First Year

• Your assigned accounts have clear action plans, reliable records, and consistent follow-up.

• Collection performance improves against agreed targets, with overdue balances and disputes addressed promptly.

• Customers and internal partners receive clear answers and dependable service.

• You use AI and process improvements to reduce manual work while maintaining accuracy and financial controls.

You Should Have

• Strong performance and ownership of results in work, school, or projects you’ve pursued.

• The ability to learn unfamiliar processes and systems quickly, ask thoughtful questions, and apply feedback.

• Clear written and verbal communication, attention to detail, and the judgment to handle sensitive conversations professionally.

• Persistence and initiative: you follow up, find practical ways to resolve issues, and take responsibility for results.

• The ability to work independently and with others, manage competing priorities, and stay organized as workloads change.

• Hands-on experience using generative AI to research, analyze, or improve a recurring task. You can explain how you used it and checked the results.

• Strong problem-solving skills: you can investigate a discrepancy, identify what is missing, and follow the issue through resolution.

• Sound judgment about AI output and confidential data. You verify facts and figures, recognize when an answer is unreliable, and know when to seek human review.

• Comfort working with numbers and spreadsheets. You can organize information, spot inconsistencies, and learn the Excel or Google Sheets tools needed to investigate account balances.

• Collections, finance, customer service, and experience with NetSuite, Tesorio, or Stripe are helpful but optional.

The opportunity:

As part of the EMEA Accounting team in Amsterdam, we are opening a role for an Operations Controller – a hands-on leader for accounting, control, and finance automation across 15+ countries. This is an opportunity to build modern finance operations in a fast-growing multinational environment, as part of a team that is shaping and learning from the new world of autonomous finance firsthand; a genuinely unique opportunity to get ahead of the market. The role requires a strong grasp of financial reporting and VAT principles, sharp analytical thinking, and the professional judgment needed to lead across stakeholders and time zones under pressure.

You will:

• Own full monthly close timeliness, completeness and accuracy across a growing multi-entity footprint, overseeing standardized schedules and checklists that scale as entity count grows.

• Own accuracy of local Revenue and COGS, including transfer pricing calculations based on approved methodology.

• Control cost, balance sheet and liquidity through among others OPEX and T&E challenge, financial anomaly investigation, deposits and cash flow review.

• Build and deliver automation roadmap for the Accounting function within and outside the ERP by identifying manual, repeatable work and sequencing its removal.

• Enforce correct output and input VAT recording end-to-end, based on strong technical acumen on EU and international VAT principles.

• Drive corrective actions across internal and external stakeholders to enforce correct financial and VAT accountingImplement e-invoicing readiness for local continuous transaction control mandates.

• Partnership with Business to capture new commercial models and contract structures before they hit the ledger, embedding them into standard accounting workflows; with FP&A to sharpen figures and inputs feeding their reporting models; and with other back office functions (Legal, People, Workplace) on recurring compliance, bookings, and ad hoc initiatives.

• Provide leadership through supervising and developing the Accounting team.

You should have:

• 5+ years of progressive accounting and operational finance experience in a high-growth company.

• Experience working in a multinational setting with cross-border reporting needs.

• Strong background in GAAP, financial reporting and ERP systems.

• Proven experience with applying VAT rules and VAT accounting across Europe.

• Top level proficiency in deploying and overseeing automated finance tools, agent frameworks and modern financial data stacks.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills to coordinate across departments and manage external relationships.

• Exceptional organizational, prioritization and planning skills, and keen attention to detail.

What is in it for you:

• An opportunity to contribute to one of the fastest-growing companies, where you’ll have the chance to create a global impact while being a part of a thriving multinational environment.

• Daily catered lunches incl. vegetarian options, breakfast, snacks and soft drinks available in our office on daily basis.

• Commute expenses: Flexport will cover home-office commuting costs for employees living outside of Amsterdam.

• Amazing office in the heart of Amsterdam.

• 25 working days as vacation days based on full time employment.

• Health insurance: Flexport offers a collective health insurance plan including a basic package and any available additional packages. Your monthly premium is fully paid by Flexport.

• A defined pension contribution scheme.

• Equity program: every team member becomes a shareholder, aligning our success with yours. As a private company in a multi-trillion dollar industry, you have a direct stake in our collective growth and success.

• Employee Assistance Program through Aetna Resources for Living: Flexport provides an employer-sponsored program at no cost to you and your household members.

• Parental leave benefit: Flexport is here to support you and your families in one of the most important times in life – the birth of a child! Our parental leave program allows both mothers and partners to take time off from work for pregnancy, childbirth, and to bond with your new child.

postings.text:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

The Opportunity

As Flexport continues to grow its footprint across Asia Pacific, we're looking for a Payroll Manager to be the cornerstone of payroll excellence across the region. You'll own the full payroll cycle for our APAC entities — spanning Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, Greater China, Vietnam, Thailand, Korea, Japan, Indonesia, Cambodia, Philippines, India and other new markets as we expand — and serve as the go-to expert where precision, compliance, and people experience intersect.

Sitting within the APAC People team and reporting to the Senior Director, People APAC, this is a people-manager role leading a team of one, with significant cross-functional visibility. You'll set the regional payroll operating standard, drive payroll strategy, build out your team as scale demands, and work closely with Finance, People Operations, and business partners to ensure every employee across APAC is paid accurately and on time.

What You'll Do

- Own Regional Payroll End to End: Lead monthly payroll processing across 18+ APAC entities, managing vendor relationships and ensuring timely, accurate execution at scale.

- Handle Direct Payroll Execution: Perform hands-on processing and verification for assigned entities, directly coordinating with payroll vendors to calculate and finalize local payroll runs.

- Lead & Develop the Team: Manage and grow a direct report responsible for payroll data preparation — set priorities, review quality, and build a team structure that scales with new-market growth.

- Drive Data Accuracy: Coordinate with Finance on payment funding, GL booking, cost centre allocation, and month-end reconciliations — keeping payroll and finance in lockstep.

- Support the Full Employee Lifecycle: Own off-cycle payments, bonus runs, and statutory pay calculations across all employment events, ensuring compliance with local labour requirements.

- Enable Compliant Growth: Partner with the Expansion team to onboard new APAC entities onto payroll — from vendor setup to first run — as Flexport enters new markets.

- Support on regional bonus scheme: partner with global and regional stakeholders on incentive plan.

- Be the Audit & Compliance Expert: Own external audit requests, maintain payroll documentation standards, and manage compliance notifications as the business evolves.

- Elevate Vendor Performance: Own vendor SLA performance across a large multi-vendor footprint, proactively resolving service issues and driving consistent quality across all markets.

- Own Leave & Statutory Pay Calculations: Calculate maternity, paternity, sick, and other statutory leave pay amounts across all APAC entities, coordinating with People Ops on eligibility determination.

- Manage Overtime Compliance: Ensure accurate, compliant overtime calculations across markets with strict statutory multiplier requirements.

- Administer Post-Employment Payments: Process ongoing non-compete payments and other post-termination obligations, tracking start and stop dates for accuracy.

- Execute Compensation Changes: Process merit increases and promotions once approved, including any required backpay adjustments, accurately and on schedule.

- Lead Annual Compliance Cycles: Own annual individual income tax reconciliation and social insurance/housing fund base adjustments across applicable markets.

- Manage Equity-Related Withholding: Handle tax withholding and reporting obligations triggered by RSU vesting events across jurisdictions.

What We're Looking For

- 8+ years of hands-on APAC payroll experience, including 3+ years managing/leading a team, and demonstrated ownership of 5+ countries' payroll operations at scale (ideally 10+).

- Broad multi-country payroll experience across the region — Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, Greater China, Vietnam, Thailand, Korea, Japan, Indonesia, Cambodia, Philippines, India — with a track record of standing up new-market payroll from scratch.

- Deep knowledge of statutory compliance, local labour laws, and payroll vendor management across a large, diverse APAC footprint.

- Proven people-management experience — able to coach, delegate, and build capability in a small but scaling team.

- Hands-on experience using modern AI assistants to automate data analysis, reporting, and modelling.

- Proven ability to partner with Finance on reconciliations, GL allocations, and audit deliverables.

- A reputation for precision — you hold yourself and your team to a high bar and catch issues before they reach employees.

- Strong communicator who can work fluidly across Finance, People Operations, and People Business Partners.

- Experience with HRIS platforms, specifically Workday.

- Professional proficiency in English is a MUST.

- Energised by a fast-scaling environment and excited to build payroll infrastructure and a team from the ground up in new markets.

- Comfortable challenging ideas and holding space for other perspectives to be heard.

- Strong logical approach to resolving complex issues and adept at fostering resilience.

- Committed to maintaining a high degree of personal integrity and confidentiality.

This role is focused on operational excellence and AI-enabled transformation: the ideal candidate combines deep AP domain expertise with the ability to identify, build, and deploy practical automation and agentic AI solutions that materially improve efficiency, accuracy, and scalability. • Experience establishing and maintaining internal controls, compliance frameworks, and process improvements.

• Experience operating in a high-growth, global logistics, freight, or supply chain environment.

postings.title: Senior Manager, Accounts Receivable
postings.text:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

About the Role

Flexport is seeking a Senior AR Manager to lead the APAC accounts receivable function as part of our 2026 initiative to modernize and scale the global AR organization. This role owns cash collection performance, past-due backlog reduction, and credit block (CB) mitigation across the region, while driving automation and AI-enabled process improvements that align with Flexport's global standards.

The ideal candidate is metrics-driven, comfortable managing high-volume, multi-entity, multi-currency operations, and skilled at building strong cross-functional and client relationships.

Key Responsibilities

• Own the end-to-end AR performance for APAC, including DSO, collections effectiveness, and past-due/aging targets, reporting results against KPIs on a weekly and monthly cadence to global finance leadership.

• Drive down past-due backlog through structured collection strategies, escalation protocols, and proactive cash application, with a focus on converting outstanding AR into cash faster.

• Lead automation and AI tech initiatives across the AR workflow (dunning, cash application, reconciliation, reporting) to reduce manual touchpoints and improve throughput, in partnership with Systems/RevOps.

• Partner with Billing, Operations, and client-facing (Sales/Account Management/CS) teams to resolve complex, multi-entity reconciliations and root-cause recurring disputes.

• Mitigate credit block (CB) by identifying trends, tightening controls with Billing/Ops upstream, and implementing preventive process changes.

• Ensure full compliance with Flexport's global AR policies, SOX/internal controls, and regional regulatory requirements, maintaining data integrity across systems.

• Lead, coach, and motivate a regional AR team, setting clear individual KPIs, running performance reviews, and building a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

• Standardize APAC processes to Flexport's global playbook while adapting for local client and regulatory nuances.

• Present regional AR health, risks, and improvement plans to senior finance stakeholders, including escalation of at-risk accounts.

• Support systems implementations, UAT, and process documentation tied to AR automation projects.

KPIs / Success Metrics

• DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) and past-due percentage of total AR

• Collections-to-target ratio and cash applied vs. cash forecasted

• Chargeback rate and dispute resolution cycle time

• Reconciliation aging and accuracy (unapplied cash, unallocated credits)

• Team productivity and adherence to Flexport service-level standards

• Automation adoption / reduction in manual processing hours

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field (CPA/CMA a plus)

• 8+ years in Accounts Receivable/Credit & Collections, including 3+ years managing teams, ideally within a Shared Service Center or multi-entity, multi-region environment

• Proven track record reducing past-due AR and improving DSO in a high-volume, fast-paced setting

• Experience partnering cross-functionally with Billing, Operations, and client-facing teams to resolve disputes and reconciliations

• Strong working knowledge of ERP/AR systems (e.g., NetSuite, Oracle, SAP) and experience driving automation or AI-enabled process improvement (RPA, OCR, workflow tools)

• Data-driven mindset with strong Excel/BI reporting skills; comfortable building and defending KPI dashboards

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills; able to influence stakeholders across levels and regions

• APAC market/regulatory exposure preferred; multilingual a plus

• Demonstrated people leadership: coaching, performance management, and team morale-building

• Committed to data integrity, ethical business practices, and 100% accuracy standards

Key Responsibilities

China Statutory Tax Compliance

• Manage and file all required PRC statutory tax filings (CIT, VAT, stamp duty) in-house, in line with local market and city-specific requirements.

• Monitor filing deadlines across all China entities/locations and ensure timely, accurate submission.

• Track changes in PRC tax law and regulations and assess their impact on the business.

• Lead or assist with the annual CIT reconciliation and annual statutory tax filing process.

• Respond to tax bureau inquiries, audits, and information requests.

APAC Tax Reconciliation

• Manage and lead the tax reconciliation process across APAC entities, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and timely close.

• Partner with regional finance teams to identify and resolve reconciliation discrepancies.

• Provide regular reporting on APAC tax positions and risk exposure to the APAC Regional Controller.

Tax Advisory and Process Improvement

• Advise business stakeholders on APAC tax compliance requirements and implications of new transactions or business changes.

• Identify and drive improvements to tax compliance processes, controls, and reporting workflows, including automation opportunities.

External Stakeholder Management

• Liaise with local accounting firms, tax agents, and advisors across APAC markets to manage outsourced tax compliance work.

• Manage scope, quality, cost, and timeliness of external tax service providers.

• Coordinate transfer pricing documentation (local file, master file, and related filings) with external advisors and the regional/group transfer pricing team.

• Support indirect tax (VAT/GST) and direct tax matters across the region, including planning, compliance, and dispute resolution.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Taxation, or a related field.

• 5–8 years of relevant China tax experience, ideally including exposure to APAC regional tax matters; background in a Big 4 or professional accounting firm is a plus.

• Solid working knowledge of PRC tax laws and regulations and general familiarity with tax regimes across other APAC markets.

• Practical experience with transfer pricing documentation and indirect tax compliance.

• Proven experience managing relationships with external tax agents, accounting firms, or advisors across multiple jurisdictions.

• Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail.

• Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and operate effectively in a fast-paced, multi-country environment.

Responsibilities:

• Oversee bank relationships and implement efficient banking strategies.

• Implement and manage treasury management systems.

• Foster a positive and collaborative work environment.

• Proven ability to manage complex financial transactions.

We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

About the Team

The Treasury function manages regional cash liquidity, payments, and banking relationships across 16 APAC entities and 33+ bank accounts (JPM, HSBC, BOC, ICBC, CMB, DBS, IBK, ABA).

Job Summary

Flexport is hiring a Treasury Analyst to own execution of APAC's regular and emergency bill payments across host-to-host and manual bank channels for all APAC entities — and to support the Senior Treasury & Payment Analyst on bank reconciliation, cashflow forecasting, and bank guarantee administration. This is a foundational treasury role suited to someone early in their treasury or banking operations career who wants exposure to a fast-growing, multi-entity, multi-currency environment.

Key Responsibilities

• Process regular weekly and emergency/ad hoc bill payments for all APAC entities via host-to-host (~80% of volume) and manual bank portal execution (~20%).

• Review and verify bill payment details before setting payments, including country-specific tax checks (e.g., Thailand VAT/WHT verification for eWHT certificates), to ensure accuracy before submission.

• Compile and submit payment lists to the US team for approval, then execute approved payments in NetSuite and JPM (and other banking portals).

• Support monthly bank reconciliation across ~33 APAC bank accounts ahead of month-end close.

• Support cashflow monitoring and forecasting across the 16 entities the Treasury team covers.

• Support administration of Flexport APAC bank guarantees, including tracking renewals and coordinating documentation requests.

• Support new bank account opening for geo-expansion markets (upcoming China Ningbo, New Zealand) — preparing documentation, application forms, and KYC materials.

• Support to maintain and update banking documentation, including authorized signer lists, director/legal representative records, and bank callback lists.

• Partner with AR, AP, and Accounting to resolve discrepancies between bank data, NetSuite, and Core.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field.

• 1-3 years of experience in payment processing, treasury, or banking operations.

• Comfortable working across multiple banking portals and high daily payment volumes with strong attention to detail and accuracy under deadline pressure.

• Strong Excel skills; experience with NetSuite or similar ERP systems is a plus.

• Proficiency in Mandarin and English, both written and spoken, to support regional stakeholders and local bank relationships.

• Organized and reliable with recurring, deadline-driven processes (daily/weekly payment cycles, month-end close).
